segments.t: In his hospital room, Mathias is discharged with a portable heart monitor following a terrifying heart attack. When ruthless producer Igor de Serisy storms in to drag him immediately to a meeting, Noemie erupts in righteous fury to defend Mathias's life. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Le médecin t'a posé ce moniteur?
Oui, pour surveiller mon rythme cardiaque.
Tu dois te reposer à la maison.
Igor veut aller chez le réalisateur.
Tu as failli mourir d'un infarctus!
C'est un rendez-vous très important aujourd'hui.
Igor traite tout le monde sans pitié.
Il m'a quand même apporté des chocolats.
Ne cherche pas à le défendre encore!
Je ne veux pas perdre ce projet.
Ta vie vaut plus que ce film.
Tu es vraiment en colère, ma chérie.
Je refuse de te laisser mourir bêtement.
Rentrons chez nous nous reposer ensemble.
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Le médecin t'a posé ce moniteur?
'Did the doctor place this monitor on you?' Noemie examines the device on Mathias's chest. The compound past verb t'a posé introduces the medical context.
Oui, pour surveiller mon rythme cardiaque.
'Yes, to monitor my heart rate.' Mathias explains the safeguard. The infinitive phrase pour surveiller states the clinical purpose.
Tu dois te reposer à la maison.
'You must rest at home.' Noemie insists on immediate convalescence. The reflexive verb te reposer emphasizes personal recovery.
Igor veut aller chez le réalisateur.
'Igor wants to go to the director's house.' Mathias nervously mentions the meeting. The prepositional phrase chez le réalisateur identifies the proposed stop.
Tu as failli mourir d'un infarctus!
'You almost died of a heart attack!' Noemie reminds him of how close he came to death. The verb phrase as failli mourir highlights the life-or-death stakes.
C'est un rendez-vous très important aujourd'hui.
'It is a very important meeting today.' Mathias struggles with workplace duty. The adjective phrase très important reflects his chronic anxiety.
Igor traite tout le monde sans pitié.
'Igor treats everyone without mercy.' Noemie condemns the producer's exploitation. The prepositional phrase sans pitié describes ruthless abuse.
Il m'a quand même apporté des chocolats.
'He still brought me chocolates.' Mathias offers a pathetic defense of his partner. The conjunction quand même grasps at superficial kindness.
Ne cherche pas à le défendre encore!
'Do not try to defend him again!' Noemie cuts through his excuses. The negative imperative ne cherche pas refuses compromise.
Je ne veux pas perdre ce projet.
'I do not want to lose this project.' Mathias admits his fear of failure. The negative structure ne veux pas perdre captures commercial panic.
Ta vie vaut plus que ce film.
'Your life is worth more than this film.' Noemie reestablishes human priorities. The comparative expression vaut plus que puts work below health.
Tu es vraiment en colère, ma chérie.
'You are truly angry, my darling.' Mathias feels both chastised and deeply loved. The prepositional phrase en colère registers her passionate defense.
Je refuse de te laisser mourir bêtement.
'I refuse to let you die stupidly.' Noemie stands between him and exhaustion. The adverb bêtement rejects unnecessary self-destruction.
Rentrons chez nous nous reposer ensemble.

'Let us go home to rest together.' Mathias surrenders to love and good sense. The imperative verb rentrons promises recovery and peace. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Mathias smiles gently and takes Noemie's hand, grateful for her fierce love and protective strength.
